targets.authors: Lazaraton, A., Riggenbach, H., & Ediger, A.
targets.title: Forming a discipline: Applied linguists’ literacy in research methodology and statistics.
targets.evidence_quote:
The current study seeks to

partially replicate Lazaraton et al.’s study in an attempt to assess the current state of statistical

targets.outcome_quote:
In spite of these limitations, the current study demonstrates that quantitative methodology

remains an important component of applied linguistics/SLA. In many respects, the findings are

not sharply different from those found by Lazaraton et al. over 25 years ago, even though

numerous recent publications have highlighted the importance of sound quantitative

methodology (e.g., Cunnings, 2012; Ellis, 2000; Larson-Hall, 2010; Plonksy & Gass, 2011).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors summarize the findings as not sharply different from the target after 25 years. Comparisons also describe similar course counts, largely consistent knowledge rankings, and persistently positive attitudes. The overall comparison supports successful despite qualified differences in training adequacy. Other cited surveys provide context; the self-efficacy paper supplies a measure, rather than a separately retested finding.

reasoning: A new survey partially retests the published statistical-literacy survey of Lazaraton and colleagues; direct comparisons to that target are reported.
